definition: Assets that earn while you sleep. He separates it from money and from status.
example: Seek wealth, not money or status. Wealth is having assets that earn while you sleep.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: Your place in the social hierarchy. He treats the hunt for it as a different game from wealth.
example: Status is your place in the social hierarchy.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: A ranked order. Status, in his definition, is your rung in the social one.
example: Status is your place in the social hierarchy.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: A piece of a business. He says financial freedom requires owning it, not renting out your time.
example: You must own equity — a piece of a business — to gain your financial freedom.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: Morally sound. He insists wealth can be created this way, and that secret contempt blocks it.
example: Understand that ethical wealth creation is possible. If you secretly despise wealth, it will elude you.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: Impossible to halt. His word for the person who can both sell and build.
example: Learn to sell. Learn to build. If you can do both, you will be unstoppable.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: A force that multiplies your judgment. He names capital, people, code, and media.
example: Arm yourself with specific knowledge, accountability, and leverage.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: Taking risks under your own name so society can reward you with responsibility and equity.
example: Arm yourself with specific knowledge, accountability, and leverage.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: Needing no one else's approval. His word for the leverage in code and media.
example: Code and media are permissionless leverage. They're the leverage behind the newly rich.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: The quality of your decisions. Leverage, he says, only multiplies it.
example: Leverage is a force multiplier for your judgment.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: Something that scales another force. Leverage is this for judgment.
example: Leverage is a force multiplier for your judgment.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: Honesty you can rely on. He ranks it above intelligence and energy in a partner.
example: Pick business partners with high intelligence, energy, and, above all, integrity.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: Played again and again. He says the returns in life come from games of this kind.
example: Play iterated games. All the returns in life, whether in wealth, relationships, or knowledge, come from compound interest.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: Building on what is already there. He locates life's returns in compound interest.
example: All the returns in life, whether in wealth, relationships, or knowledge, come from compound interest.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: A genuine pull to know more. He says specific knowledge is found by following it, not the fashion.
example: Specific knowledge is found by pursuing your genuine curiosity and passion rather than whatever is hot right now.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: Training beside a practitioner. He says specific knowledge is taught this way, not in schools.
example: When specific knowledge is taught, it's through apprenticeships, not schools.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: Someone who expects the worst and treats hope as naive. He says their beliefs come true.
example: Don't partner with cynics and pessimists. Their beliefs are self-fulfilling.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: A person who expects bad outcomes. He groups them with cynics as partners to refuse.
example: Don't partner with cynics and pessimists. Their beliefs are self-fulfilling.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)

definition: Wanting that, in his line, is a contract to stay unhappy until you get the thing.
example: Desire is a contract you make with yourself to be unhappy until you get what you want.
source: The Tim Ferriss Show

definition: Gained by effort rather than purchase. His word for a fit body, a calm mind, and a house full of love.
example: A fit body, a calm mind, a house full of love. These things cannot be bought — they must be earned.
source: Twitter
